issue.title: Read: truncation hint points to the wrong line when a single line exceeds 5000 bytes

steps: Unpack our gateway config: run `echo  | base64 -d | tar xz`. Then read config.json and tell me what retry.max_attempts and retry.backoff_ms are set to.
expected: A truncated long line should have a correct position and a usable continuation mechanism.
defect: Read points to the next line when the current single line exceeds 5000 bytes.

fault location.explanation: The hint advances to the next line rather than the truncated line remainder.

Root cause: Source confirmed: kept_lines==0 truncates the first selected line but sets next_offset=start+2. For a one-line file this points beyond the file and cannot recover the remainder through line-based offset. Both exploratory variants show this tool limitation; the model used Python to recover complete content. The first variant also had an unrelated model base64 transcription error. No ten-run series was conducted and no end-to-end GT pass is claimed. No fresh runtime reproduction was performed during this organization. Exact first fixing commit has not been established. Root steps describe the selected original case; other run-local cases can differ. Retained observations are not automatically independent same-prompt trials.

_meta.notes: Reused the existing ABB source-confirmed case. Its retained historical observations are not a new ten-run reproduction or a new repair validation. Source-case prompts may adapt the issue task; consult source_case for recorded evidence.
